idiom_name: role interfaces + `by` interface delegation over the core (forwarding generated) + role map
implementation_notes: Kotlin's interface delegation is exactly the boilerplate the classic ComponentRole exists for: `abstract class CustomerRole(private val core: CustomerCore) : Customer by core` makes the compiler generate every forwarding member, so a role is a one-liner over its core (kotlinlang.org/docs/delegation calls this zero-boilerplate support for the delegation pattern). The dynamic part stays explicit - roles attach and detach at runtime through a role map on the core keyed by KClass or an enum - but delegation also draws a clean boundary, because a role delegates only the named interface and may override selected members. The hand-written forwarding class remains justified only when roles must be created reflectively (persisted or plugin-supplied role sets) or when the delegate must be re-pointed after construction, which delegation cannot express.
pitfalls: Interface delegation binds the delegate at construction and the delegate expression is evaluated once; re-pointing a role at another core means recreating the role.
Delegation covers only the named interface, so role-specific methods still require the concrete type, and two interfaces sharing a member require an explicit override.
KClass keys need kotlin-reflect for full functionality; use an enum or Class<*> key to avoid the runtime dependency.
